what_makes_it_distinct: The largest curated archive of humanitarian situation reports and operational maps, searchable by crisis, country and source.

what_makes_it_distinct: Rapid, event by event attribution that pairs climate modelling with an analysis of who was exposed and why.

what_makes_it_distinct: An early digital native newspaper in Latin America, still reporting on El Salvador from exile.

what_makes_it_distinct: Harmonized statistics with matching NUTS boundary files, so European regional data can be mapped directly.

name: IStories (Важные истории)

what_makes_it_distinct: Exile reporters combining leaked Russian databases with cross border partners to document the hidden costs of the war.

name: International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED)

modifier_reason: Adaptation and informal urbanism research with Global South partners
description: IIED is an independent policy research institute founded in 1971 by Barbara Ward and based in London, working with partner organizations across Africa, Asia and Latin America. Use its briefings and the journal Environment and Urbanization for evidence on adaptation finance, informal settlements, land rights and locally led adaptation.
what_makes_it_distinct: Decades of partner led research on informal settlements and locally led adaptation, including the journal Environment and Urbanization.

name: Made in China Journal

modifier_reason: Fills the labour and China gap; open access academic
description: Made in China Journal is an open access publication from ANU Press, edited by Ivan Franceschini and Nicholas Loubere, on labour, civil society and rights in China and in Chinese projects abroad. Read its themed issues for scholarly essays written to be understood outside academia.

name: Mediapart

modifier_reason: Reader funded with nonprofit ownership; French accountability reporting in depth

what_makes_it_distinct: A subscriber funded daily with no advertising whose capital is locked in a nonprofit fund to prevent takeover.

name: Natural Hazards Center

what_makes_it_distinct: Turns fresh fieldwork from recent disasters into short, practitioner ready findings within months.

name: Nouveau Projet

what_makes_it_distinct: Quebec's independent magazine of long essays, published by a small Montreal house that also issues books and plays.

name: RFI (Radio France Internationale)

what_makes_it_distinct: The deepest daily radio coverage of Francophone Africa, alongside Chinese, Spanish and Russian services.

what_makes_it_distinct: A university group producing English and French scholarship devoted solely to the six Francophone Sahel states.

name: Spacing
format: Print magazine, city blogs, podcast, books
modifier_reason: Canadian urbanism gap; independent publisher
description: Spacing is an independent Toronto magazine about Canadian cities, covering public space, transit, planning, housing and urban design in print and through city blogs. Use it for locally informed writing on how Canadian streets, parks and neighbourhoods are planned and contested.
what_makes_it_distinct: A print magazine devoted entirely to the public realm of Canadian cities.

name: The Markup
modifier_reason: Nonprofit newsroom with open methods on technology accountability
description: The Markup is a nonprofit newsroom, part of CalMatters since 2024, that investigates how technology companies and algorithms affect people, publishing its data and methods with each story. what_makes_it_distinct: Publishes a full methodology, and often the code and data, behind each technology investigation.

name: Urbanisme
modifier_reason: French planning culture; fills a gap
description: Urbanisme is a French review published since 1932 that debates cities, territories, housing, mobility and ecological transition with planners, architects and researchers. Read it in French for European planning debates that rarely reach English language outlets.
what_makes_it_distinct: Nearly a century of French debate on the city, with planners, architects and geographers in the same pages.

name: AOC (Analyse Opinion Critique)
modifier_reason: Subscriber funded French ideas daily written by researchers
description: AOC is an independent French online daily of ideas founded in 2018 by Sylvain Bourmeau, publishing one analysis, one opinion and one critique each day by researchers, writers and artists. Use it for considered French language essays on politics, society, ecology, technology and culture.
what_makes_it_distinct: Three long texts a day by academics and writers, and nothing else.

name: Agência Pública
modifier_reason: Nonprofit investigative depth on Brazil, with open republication
description: Agência Pública is a Brazilian nonprofit investigative journalism agency founded in 2011 by women reporters and funded by foundations and readers. Read its investigations on the Amazon, land conflict, labour and state power in Portuguese, or in the Spanish and English versions it offers, all under an open republication licence.
what_makes_it_distinct: Publishes every investigation under an open licence so other Brazilian and foreign outlets can reprint it.

name: Caribbean Investigative Journalism Network
modifier_reason: Underserved Caribbean geography plus nonprofit ownership
description: The Caribbean Investigative Journalism Network is a nonprofit project of the Media Institute of the Caribbean that funds, trains and publishes journalists across the islands. Use it for collaborative investigations into corruption, climate vulnerability, public health and finance in Caribbean states that rarely receive sustained international coverage.
what_makes_it_distinct: The only regional network producing investigations across islands by Caribbean journalists for Caribbean audiences.

name: Disclose

what_makes_it_distinct: A fully open journal of record for digital humanities, published with no author or reader fees.

modifier_reason: Critical geography gap; open companion magazine widens access

Use it for reporting on Indian politics, civil liberties, caste, labour and media freedom, keeping in mind the Meta stories it retracted in 2022.
what_makes_it_distinct: India's best known reader funded nonprofit newsroom, repeatedly sued over reporting critical of the government.

name: arXiv
format: Preprints, daily listings, RSS feeds, API
modifier_reason: Primary evidence source run as academic infrastructure
description: arXiv is the open access preprint repository founded by Paul Ginsparg in 1991 and operated by Cornell Tech, hosting more than two million papers in physics, mathematics, computer science, statistics and related fields. Use subject feeds such as cs.AI, cs.CV and cs.CY to see research before peer review.
what_makes_it_distinct: The primary open repository where machine learning and physical science research appears months before journal publication.

name: oDR (openDemocracy Russia and Beyond)
modifier_reason: Section of openDemocracy with reduced, unconfirmed current output
description: The Russia and Eurasia section of the London nonprofit openDemocracy, publishing reporting and analysis by local writers on civil society, labour, protest and repression across the former Soviet space. Use its archive and any new pieces for grassroots perspectives, and confirm how active the section remains before relying on it.
what_makes_it_distinct: Local activists, researchers and journalists from Russia, Ukraine, the Caucasus and Central Asia writing for an English readership.

name: Apollo Magazine
modifier_reason: Overlaps The Art Newspaper; collector oriented prestige
description: Apollo is a London art magazine founded in 1925, covering museums, exhibitions, art history, architecture, heritage and the art market in monthly issues and online. Read it for exhibition reviews, museum politics and collection histories, with a perspective closer to curators and collectors than to contemporary theory.
what_makes_it_distinct: A monthly founded a century ago that joins art historical scholarship with reporting on museums and collecting.

name: BBC News Arabic (بي بي سي نيوز عربي)
modifier_reason: Language service of the BBC, which is already listed
description: BBC News Arabic is the Arabic language service of the BBC World Service, publishing online and on television for audiences across the Middle East and North Africa. Use it through browser translation to see how regional stories are framed for Arabic speakers, alongside BBC English coverage.
what_makes_it_distinct: The oldest foreign language service of the BBC, broadcasting in Arabic since 1938.

name: CityGeographics
modifier_reason: Urban cartography practice; one author, infrequent posts
description: Personal research blog of Duncan A. Smith of the Centre for Advanced Spatial Analysis at University College London, on urban form, density and interactive mapping. Use it for worked examples of city scale data visualization and for the open web maps he builds; posts are infrequent.
what_makes_it_distinct: An urban geographer's own notebook of interactive city maps, with methods explained alongside results.

name: EUobserver
modifier_reason: Nonprofit alternative to Politico Europe on the same beat
description: EUobserver is an independent nonprofit news site founded in Brussels in 2000 that reports on European Union institutions, migration, rule of law, foreign policy and lobbying. Use it as a smaller, reader supported counterweight to Politico Europe when following European policy that affects Canada, Switzerland or the United Kingdom.
what_makes_it_distinct: A nonprofit Brussels newsroom with no corporate owner covering European Union institutions.

name: Economy and Society
modifier_reason: Adds academic political economy depth
description: Economy and Society is a peer reviewed quarterly published by Routledge, founded in 1972, covering economic sociology, political economy, governmentality and the social study of finance. Consult it for theoretical articles behind current debates on labour, markets and the state, mostly through library access.
what_makes_it_distinct: A long running home for governmentality studies and the sociology of finance and markets.

name: Journal of Urban Technology
modifier_reason: Scholarly urban technology niche; paywalled commercial publisher
description: The Journal of Urban Technology is a peer reviewed journal published by Routledge, part of Taylor & Francis, on how digital and physical technologies shape cities, planning and urban governance. Use it for scholarly studies of smart cities, urban data and infrastructure, mostly through a library subscription.
what_makes_it_distinct: A long running scholarly journal devoted specifically to technology in cities, including critical studies of smart city programs.

name: Just Security
owner: Reiss Center on Law and Security, New York University School of Law
format: Analysis articles, document trackers, podcast, newsletter
modifier_reason: Overlaps Lawfare and EJIL: Talk! on law and security
description: Just Security is an online forum on national security, international law and human rights based at the Reiss Center on Law and Security at New York University School of Law. Use it for expert analysis of the law of armed conflict, sanctions, accountability and technology governance.
what_makes_it_distinct: Legal analysis written by practitioners and scholars, with document trackers and timelines for major cases.

name: Los Angeles Review of Books (LARB)
format: Essays, reviews, interviews, quarterly print journal, podcast
modifier_reason: Nonprofit review; partly overlaps other book reviews listed
description: A nonprofit review founded in 2011 by Tom Lutz in Los Angeles, publishing daily essays, interviews and criticism online alongside a quarterly print journal. Use it for long reviews of new work in philosophy, history, technology and the arts written by scholars for general readers, from a West Coast vantage.
what_makes_it_distinct: A member funded review built online first, giving academic authors long space outside the New York and London review circuit.

name: Mousse Magazine
format: Print magazine, essays, interviews, exhibition coverage, books
modifier_reason: Curatorial depth from an independent Italian publisher
description: Mousse is a Milan based contemporary art magazine and publishing house founded in 2006, printing its issues in English and posting exhibition documentation online most days. Use it for extended conversations with artists and curators and for a running survey of exhibitions across Europe and beyond.
what_makes_it_distinct: Extended artist and curator conversations alongside a daily visual record of exhibitions worldwide.

name: Tempo (Cambridge Music Journal)
format: Peer reviewed articles, performance, recording and book reviews
modifier_reason: Academic journal for new music; narrow fit with the themes
description: Tempo is a quarterly journal of new music founded in 1939 as the house magazine of the publisher Boosey & Hawkes and published since 2003 by Cambridge University Press. Use it for scholarly articles on living composers and for reviews of premieres, festivals, recordings and books in contemporary concert and experimental music.
what_makes_it_distinct: The longest running English language journal devoted to contemporary composition, mixing scholarship with reviews of first performances.

name: Terrain.org
modifier_reason: Nonprofit literary journal on place and landscape
description: Online journal of the built and natural environments, published since 1997 by the nonprofit Terrain Publishing in Tucson, Arizona. Read it for essays, poetry, fiction and interviews about place, landscape, cities and climate, with a mostly North American set of writers.
what_makes_it_distinct: A literary journal that treats cities and wild places together as one subject.

name: The East African
modifier_reason: Regional East African view absent from larger outlets
description: The East African is a weekly regional newspaper published in Nairobi by Nation Media Group, covering Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda and their neighbours. Use it for politics, trade and integration in the East African Community and for regional views of the Horn and the Great Lakes.
what_makes_it_distinct: A newspaper edited for the East African Community as one region.

name: The Gleaner (Jamaica Gleaner)
modifier_reason: Caribbean is underserved; daily paper of record for Jamaica
description: The Gleaner, founded in Kingston in 1834, is Jamaica's oldest daily newspaper and part of the publicly listed RJRGLEANER Communications Group. Use it for daily reporting on Jamaican politics, economy, hurricanes and diaspora affairs, and as one English language window on the wider Caribbean alongside Barbadian sources.
what_makes_it_distinct: One of the oldest newspapers in the Caribbean, with an archive reaching back to 1834.

name: Bachtrack
format: Concert, opera and dance reviews, event listings, interviews
modifier_reason: Performing arts listings and criticism with a French edition
description: Bachtrack is a classical music site founded in London in 2008 by David and Alison Karlin, combining a worldwide database of concert, opera and dance listings with reviews by a large network of critics. Use it to find performances in Montreal and abroad and to read reviews in English, French, German and Spanish.
what_makes_it_distinct: The largest searchable listing of live classical music, opera and dance worldwide, with reviews in four languages.

name: Brookings Institution
modifier_reason: Prestige institution adding little new perspective
description: The Brookings Institution is a Washington think tank founded in 1916 that publishes research and commentary on economics, governance, metropolitan policy, technology and foreign affairs. Use it for baseline American policy analysis and data, keeping in mind its establishment vantage point and its funding from foundations, corporations and governments.
what_makes_it_distinct: A century old general purpose American think tank, useful mainly as a baseline of establishment policy thinking.

name: Dunia (두니아)
regions: Japan and Korea / Southeast Asia / South Asia
owner: Dunia (independent newsroom; legal owner not confirmed)
modifier_reason: Independent Korean perspective on Asia; small and in a language read by translation
description: Dunia is a Korean language independent outlet, online at thedunia.org, that presents itself as investigating Asia and publishes reports, a newsletter and video. Treat it as a secondary source read through translation, useful for a Korean vantage on Asian affairs that the large English language outlets seldom provide.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Korean language newsroom devoted to investigating the rest of Asia, a vantage rarely available in other media.

name: E3G
modifier_reason: Useful diplomacy lens, partly redundant with Carbon Brief on summits
description: E3G, short for Third Generation Environmentalism, is an independent climate change think tank founded in 2004 with offices in London, Brussels, Berlin and Washington. Use its briefings and blog for the politics of UN climate talks, coal phase out, public finance reform and European energy security.
what_makes_it_distinct: Political economy reading of climate diplomacy, with frequent briefings around UN climate summits.

name: Heatmap News
modifier_reason: Overlaps climate nonprofits already listed; United States focus
description: Heatmap News is a New York based climate and energy publication launched in 2023 by editors who came from The Week and The Atlantic, with Robinson Meyer as founding executive editor. Use it for daily reporting on clean energy deployment, climate technology, permitting fights and American climate policy.
what_makes_it_distinct: A newsroom built only around the energy transition, tracking project level fights over clean energy deployment.

name: Mail & Guardian
owner: M&G Media (majority held by Media Development Investment Fund)
modifier_reason: Mission driven owner, but Southern Africa is outside priority geographies
description: A Johannesburg weekly newspaper and daily website founded in 1985 as the Weekly Mail, majority owned since 2017 by the nonprofit Media Development Investment Fund. Use it for investigative and political coverage of South Africa and its neighbours, a region outside the reader's core priorities.
what_makes_it_distinct: A weekly born in opposition to apartheid that still anchors accountability reporting in South Africa.

name: TaiwanPlus
owner: Taiwan Public Television Service Foundation (funded by the Ministry of Culture)
format: Video news, streaming channel, documentaries, articles
modifier_reason: English Taiwan video; partly overlaps Focus Taiwan and Taipei Times
description: Taiwan's publicly funded English language video news platform, launched in 2021 with Ministry of Culture funding and operated by the Public Television Service. Use it for accessible daily video on Taiwanese politics, society and cross strait affairs, and read it as a view from Taiwan's public sector alongside independent outlets.
what_makes_it_distinct: An English language television news service produced in Taiwan for an international audience with public funding.

name: Tortoise Media
modifier_reason: Now folded into The Observer; overlaps United Kingdom anchors
description: Tortoise Media is a London company founded in 2019 by James Harding and Matthew Barzun around slow news, investigative podcasts and data indices. It bought The Observer from Guardian Media Group in 2025 and now publishes mainly under that title, so the reader should follow The Observer for its journalism.
what_makes_it_distinct: A slow news startup built on narrative podcasts that went on to take over Britain's oldest Sunday newspaper.

name: Wired
format: Articles, longform features, newsletters, podcasts, video
modifier_reason: Prestige brand overlapping other technology coverage
description: Wired is the technology magazine founded in San Francisco in 1993 and owned by Condé Nast, part of Advance Publications, with editions in Japan, Italy and Spanish speaking markets. Use it for reporting on AI, security, platforms and the politics of Silicon Valley, and skip the product reviews.
what_makes_it_distinct: Three decades of reporting on technology culture, with a Japanese edition useful for language practice.

name: e-flux
modifier_reason: Artist run publisher; adds curatorial and architecture theory
description: e-flux is a New York publishing platform founded by artist Anton Vidokle that combines paid institutional announcements with a free journal of art theory, criticism, architecture and film. Use the journal and its archive for essays on contemporary art and curatorial thinking, and skim the announcements for exhibitions.
what_makes_it_distinct: An artist run platform whose announcement service funds a free journal of theory.

name: Atmos
owner: Atmos (founded by Jake Sargent and William Defebaugh)
format: Biannual print magazine, essays, photography, newsletters, podcast
modifier_reason: Climate through art and culture; distinct from policy outlets
description: A climate and culture magazine founded in 2019 by Jake Sargent and William Defebaugh, publishing a biannual print volume and frequent online essays, photography and newsletters. Use it for visual storytelling about ecology, Indigenous knowledge, fashion and art, as a complement to policy and science reporting on climate.
what_makes_it_distinct: Treats the climate crisis as a cultural and aesthetic question through commissioned photography and art direction.

name: Disconnect
modifier_reason: Reader funded Canadian voice in technology criticism
description: Disconnect is a reader supported newsletter by Canadian technology critic Paris Marx, host of the podcast Tech Won't Save Us, offering essays on Silicon Valley, AI, platforms and digital sovereignty. Use it as a weekly critical counterweight to industry narratives, remembering that it is one author's argued position.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Canadian critic's newsletter arguing for digital sovereignty and public alternatives to United States technology firms.

name: Dissent
owner: Foundation for the Study of Independent Social Ideas
modifier_reason: Nonprofit; social democratic essays, partly overlapping other left reviews
description: Dissent is a quarterly magazine of politics and culture founded in New York in 1954 by Irving Howe and Lewis Coser and published by the nonprofit Foundation for the Study of Independent Social Ideas. Use it for long essays on labour, social democracy, feminism and international politics from the democratic left.
what_makes_it_distinct: Seven decades of democratic socialist argument opposed to both authoritarian communism and market orthodoxy.

name: Foreign Policy
modifier_reason: Overlaps Foreign Affairs and other geopolitics titles; prestige brand
description: Foreign Policy is a Washington based magazine of global affairs founded in 1970 and owned by Graham Holdings. Use it for daily analysis and argument on diplomacy, security and the world economy, with regional briefings by newsletter, while filtering its more provocative opinion headlines.
what_makes_it_distinct: Weekly regional newsletters such as China Brief and Africa Brief, each written by a named specialist.

name: International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS)
regions: Global / Europe / Southeast Asia / Middle East and North Africa
format: Reports, annual data volumes, journal, online analysis, podcasts
modifier_reason: Reference defence data; security lies outside the core themes
description: The International Institute for Strategic Studies is a London based research institute founded in 1958 that publishes The Military Balance, the journal Survival and regular strategic assessments. Use it for reference data on armed forces and defence spending, and for analysis around its Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore.
what_makes_it_distinct: The Military Balance, an annual open source inventory of armed forces and defence budgets worldwide.

name: Public Books
modifier_reason: Academic nonprofit; some overlap with other review magazines
description: Public Books is a nonprofit online magazine founded in 2012 by scholars Sharon Marcus and Caitlin Zaloom, in which academics write review essays on books, technology, cities and culture for general readers. Read it for accessible entry points into current humanities and social science debates.
what_makes_it_distinct: Academic specialists reviewing new books and ideas in plain language, edited to magazine standards.

name: War on the Rocks
modifier_reason: Practitioner view is useful but fills no priority gap
description: War on the Rocks is a Washington platform founded in 2013 by Ryan Evans, publishing analysis, commentary and podcasts on strategy, defence and foreign policy by practitioners and scholars. Use it to understand how military and policy professionals argue about conflicts that shape humanitarian operations.
what_makes_it_distinct: Defence and strategy debate written mainly by people with direct military, intelligence or policy experience.

name: World Politics
owner: Princeton Institute for International and Regional Studies (published by Johns Hopkins University Press)
modifier_reason: Prestige journal; dense, paywalled and seldom tied to the reader's fields
description: World Politics is a quarterly peer reviewed journal of comparative politics and international relations, founded in 1948 and edited at the Princeton Institute for International and Regional Studies. Use it for theory driven research on states, regimes, development and political economy, read selectively.
what_makes_it_distinct: A small number of long, heavily reviewed articles per issue that often define debates in comparative politics.

name: Actu Philosophia
modifier_reason: French language philosophy criticism is thin elsewhere in the portfolio
description: A French online review of philosophy publishing, run by a volunteer team of academics and teachers under editor Thibaut Gress, with long critical reviews and author interviews. Use it to follow new French language philosophy books across traditions, from the history of philosophy to phenomenology and analytic work.
what_makes_it_distinct: Long French reviews of new philosophy titles written by specialists, with extended author interviews, all free to read.

name: Artforum
modifier_reason: Prestige title under a corporate owner; heavy advertising
description: Artforum is a New York contemporary art magazine founded in 1962 and owned since 2022 by Penske Media Corporation, publishing criticism, exhibition reviews, essays and art world news. Use it to follow international exhibitions and critical debates, aware that advertising galleries and a corporate owner shape its field of attention.
what_makes_it_distinct: The reference record of exhibition reviews for the commercial and institutional contemporary art world since 1962.

name: Lapham's Quarterly
owner: American Agora Foundation (reported move to Bard College unverified)
format: Thematic quarterly, source excerpts, essays, podcast
modifier_reason: Unique format, but publication may be paused
description: Lapham's Quarterly is a magazine of history and ideas founded in 2007 by Lewis Lapham, with each issue assembling historical texts and new essays around one theme. Use its archive for primary source readings across centuries, and confirm its publishing status, which could not be verified here.
what_makes_it_distinct: Each issue reads one theme through excerpts from several thousand years of writing.

name: Middle East Eye
modifier_reason: Distinct regional reporting offset by opaque ownership and funding
description: Middle East Eye is a news site launched in London in 2014 and edited by David Hearst, published by M.E.E. Limited, which does not disclose its funders and denies claims of Qatari backing. Use it for reporting from Palestine, Egypt, Turkey and the Maghreb in English and French, keeping that opacity in mind.
what_makes_it_distinct: Heavy original reporting from Gaza, Egypt and the Maghreb in English and French, paired with undisclosed funding.

name: SSRN
modifier_reason: Primary source value offset by commercial publisher ownership
description: SSRN is a repository of preprints and working papers owned by Elsevier, strongest in law, economics, finance, political science and management. Use it to find research before journal publication, remembering that papers there have not been peer reviewed.
what_makes_it_distinct: The main preprint repository for law and economics working papers.

name: Semafor
regions: Global / United States / Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
modifier_reason: Venture funded generalist; mostly overlaps the larger outlets
description: Global news company founded in 2022 by Ben Smith and Justin Smith, publishing newsletters and articles that separate reported facts from the reporter's view. Use its Africa, Gulf, technology and business newsletters as a quick briefing layer, not as a source of depth.
what_makes_it_distinct: A story format that labels news, analysis and opposing views as separate sections.

name: Taipei Times
modifier_reason: Partly overlaps Focus Taiwan; editorial pages add a distinct local voice
description: Taipei Times is an English language daily founded in 1999 and owned by the Liberty Times Group, with an editorial line sympathetic to Taiwanese sovereignty. Use it for domestic politics, cross strait news and translated commentary, and its bilingual pages for parallel English and Chinese reading.
what_makes_it_distinct: Carries English translations of Liberty Times editorials and bilingual study pages alongside its own Taiwan reporting.

name: The China Project (formerly SupChina)
modifier_reason: Closed in 2023; archive only
description: The China Project, launched in New York in 2016 as SupChina by Anla Cheng and edited by Jeremy Goldkorn, published daily China news, explainers and the Sinica podcast until it closed in November 2023 for lack of funding. Use the archive for background on business, society and politics; Sinica continues independently under Kaiser Kuo.
what_makes_it_distinct: A closed outlet whose archive holds seven years of plain English explanation of Chinese society and business.

name: The Revelator
modifier_reason: Biodiversity focus, but owned by an advocacy group
description: The Revelator is an environmental news and commentary site published by the Center for Biological Diversity, an American conservation group, and edited by John R. Platt. Read it for reporting and essays on endangered species, biodiversity loss, public lands and climate, keeping its parent organisation's advocacy role in mind.
what_makes_it_distinct: An editorially separate news site funded by a conservation advocacy group, centred on wildlife and extinction.

name: Assemblage
modifier_reason: Architecture theory gap, offset by archive only status
description: Assemblage was a journal of architecture and design culture published by MIT Press from 1986 to 2000, edited by K. Michael Hays, and its 41 issues remain available through JSTOR. Use the archive for foundational debates in critical architectural theory, not for current coverage.
what_makes_it_distinct: The complete run of a journal that defined critical architecture theory in North America during the 1990s.

name: Contretemps
owner: Contretemps editorial collective (print edition with Éditions Syllepse)
modifier_reason: Collective ownership, but overlaps other left theory outlets
description: Contretemps is a French review of critical theory and politics founded in 2001 around the philosopher Daniel Bensaïd, now run mainly as a free web review by a volunteer editorial collective. Read it for Marxist, feminist, ecological and decolonial essays and translations, knowing its openly partisan line.
what_makes_it_distinct: A free French language review of Marxist theory that translates international left debates into French.

name: Lausan Collective (流傘)
modifier_reason: Volunteer collective adds diversity; output believed slow or dormant
description: A volunteer collective of writers, translators, artists and organizers from Hong Kong and its diaspora, formed during the 2019 protests and publishing in English and Chinese. Use its essays and translations for left perspectives on Hong Kong that criticize both Chinese state power and Western imperialism, and check how recently it has published.
what_makes_it_distinct: Translates Hong Kong left and labour writing between Chinese and English from an explicitly internationalist position.

name: NRC
modifier_reason: Dutch only; overlaps other European papers of record
description: NRC is a Dutch daily newspaper of record based in Amsterdam, formed in 1970 from two older liberal papers and now owned by the Belgian group Mediahuis. It publishes only in Dutch, so use it through translation for coverage of the Netherlands, European Union politics and long investigations.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Dutch paper of record with a long standing ombudsman and public corrections practice.

name: Radical Philosophy
format: Journal issues, essays, reviews, interviews, open archive
modifier_reason: Collective run and open access, with a full archive from 1972
description: Radical Philosophy is a British journal of socialist and feminist philosophy founded in 1972, run by an editorial collective and published open access since its 2018 relaunch. Use its articles and complete free archive for critical theory, continental philosophy and theoretically serious writing on borders, labour, technology and ecology.
what_makes_it_distinct: Over fifty years of socialist and feminist philosophy, with the whole archive free to read online.

name: Science Friday
format: Radio show, podcast, articles, educational resources
modifier_reason: Nonprofit audio format, offset by overlap with other science coverage
description: Science Friday is a public radio program and podcast produced by the nonprofit Science Friday Initiative, hosted since 1991 by Ira Flatow and distributed to stations by WNYC Studios. Use it as a weekly listening digest of new research in climate, health, space and technology, built on interviews with working scientists.
what_makes_it_distinct: A long running public radio science show built on direct weekly conversations with working scientists.

name: Scientific American
modifier_reason: Prestige title overlapping stronger science sources
description: Scientific American is a popular science magazine published since 1845 and owned by Springer Nature, with daily online news and a regular print edition. Use it for accessible explanations of research in climate, artificial intelligence, health and physics, checking important claims against the original papers.
what_makes_it_distinct: The oldest continuously published magazine in the United States, with working scientists among its regular authors.

name: The New Atlantis
owner: Center for the Study of Technology and Society
modifier_reason: Nonprofit; adds a perspective on technology absent elsewhere in the list
description: The New Atlantis is a quarterly journal of technology and society founded in 2003 and published in Washington by the nonprofit Center for the Study of Technology and Society. Use it for long essays on bioethics, AI, science policy and the philosophy of technology, written from a conservative humanist position unlike most technology criticism.
what_makes_it_distinct: A conservative humanist journal of technology criticism, useful as a counterweight to left and industry perspectives.

name: The Philosopher
format: Quarterly journal, essays, interviews, online events
modifier_reason: Charity owned; philosophy is otherwise well covered in the portfolio
description: The Philosopher is the journal of the Philosophical Society of England, published since 1923 and relaunched in recent years as a public philosophy quarterly with a free series of online events. Use it for accessible essays by working philosophers on politics, technology, race, ecology and the self.
what_makes_it_distinct: A century old society journal reinvented as public philosophy, pairing print issues with free live online conversations.

name: The Point
modifier_reason: Nonprofit philosophy magazine with a wide political range
description: The Point is a nonprofit magazine of philosophical essays on politics, culture and everyday life, founded in Chicago in 2009 by graduate students from the University of Chicago. Read it when you want slow, reflective essays and symposiums that ask what a good life or a good society requires.
what_makes_it_distinct: Each issue builds a symposium around one plain question about what something is for.

name: The Straits Times
modifier_reason: Top priority Southeast Asian city; establishment paper with limited independence
description: The Straits Times is Singapore's main English language daily, founded in 1845 and published by SPH Media Trust, a nonprofit entity that receives government funding. Use it for Singapore policy, business and Southeast Asian news from its regional bureaus, while reading its domestic political coverage with caution.
what_makes_it_distinct: Singapore's paper of record, with correspondents across Southeast and East Asian capitals.

name: Africanews
regions: Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
owner: Euronews SA (majority owned by Alpac Capital)
modifier_reason: Bilingual Africa baseline, but largely derived from wire copy
description: Africanews is a pan African news channel and website launched in 2016 as the sister service of Euronews, publishing parallel English and French editions. Use it as a quick continental baseline, noting that much of its report draws on agency copy and that deeper regional outlets should follow.
what_makes_it_distinct: A continent wide news service with matching English and French editions under the Euronews group.

name: France 24 Español
modifier_reason: Overlaps France 24 in French and BBC News Mundo
description: France 24 Español is the Spanish language channel and website of the French state funded broadcaster France Médias Monde, launched in September 2017 with a newsroom in Bogotá. Use it for free rolling news in Spanish with a European and Latin American outlook, as language practice alongside BBC News Mundo.
what_makes_it_distinct: A French public international channel with a Bogotá newsroom, giving Latin American news a European frame.

name: Frieze
owner: Company led by Ari Emanuel (bought from Endeavor in 2025)
modifier_reason: Prestige title tied to fair business; overlaps other art outlets
description: Frieze is a London contemporary art magazine founded in 1991, published alongside the Frieze art fairs and sold in 2025 by Endeavor to a company led by Ari Emanuel. Use it for exhibition reviews and essays on artists and curating, bearing in mind its commercial ties to the fair business.
what_makes_it_distinct: A critical magazine that shares a brand and owner with major commercial art fairs.

name: Korea JoongAng Daily
modifier_reason: Adds Korea coverage; conglomerate ownership limits the gain
description: Korea JoongAng Daily is the English language newspaper of the JoongAng Group in Seoul, founded in 2000 and distributed in Korea together with the international edition of The New York Times. Use it for South Korean politics, industry, semiconductors and culture, balanced against the centre left Hankyoreh English edition.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Korean media conglomerate's English daily, distributed together with The New York Times international edition.

name: OhmyNews (오마이뉴스)
modifier_reason: Distinct participatory model; Korean only limits use
description: OhmyNews is a South Korean online newspaper founded in 2000 by Oh Yeon-ho on the motto that every citizen is a reporter, combining staff journalists with thousands of citizen contributors. It publishes in Korean, so use it through translation for progressive and grassroots views of Korean politics.
what_makes_it_distinct: The pioneering citizen journalism newsroom, where staff editors check and publish reports from ordinary contributors.

name: Public Understanding of Science
modifier_reason: Academic source on science and society; dense and narrow
description: Public Understanding of Science is a peer reviewed journal published by SAGE since 1992 on how publics, media and institutions engage with science and technology. Use it for research on science communication, trust in expertise, risk perception and public attitudes toward emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence.
what_makes_it_distinct: A scholarly journal devoted entirely to how science is communicated, perceived and contested in public.

name: Revue des Deux Mondes
modifier_reason: Heritage title adding prestige more than new perspective
description: Revue des Deux Mondes is a French monthly review of literature, history and politics founded in 1829, now owned by Fimalac, the holding company of Marc Ladreit de Lacharrière. Use it for essays and interviews from the conservative and liberal side of French intellectual debate.
what_makes_it_distinct: One of the oldest reviews still published in Europe, with an archive reaching back to 1829.

name: Rice Media
modifier_reason: Independent Singapore voice outside state linked media
description: Rice Media is an independent Singapore digital publication founded in 2016 that publishes long features, commentary and short documentaries on social issues, class, migrant workers and culture. Use it for ground level Singaporean voices outside the state linked press, noting its uneven depth and reliance on sponsored content.
what_makes_it_distinct: Young Singaporean writers covering social life and inequality in a voice the mainstream local press seldom uses.

name: The Intercept
modifier_reason: Nonprofit status offset by overlap with investigative outlets already listed
description: The Intercept is a New York based investigative newsroom founded in 2014 with backing from Pierre Omidyar and run since 2023 as an independent nonprofit. Use it for document based reporting on surveillance, war, policing and technology companies, keeping in mind its openly adversarial stance.
what_makes_it_distinct: Built on the Snowden archive, it still specializes in leaked documents about surveillance and national security.

name: ArcGIS StoryMaps (Esri)
modifier_reason: Fills a cartographic practice gap, though it is a vendor platform
description: ArcGIS StoryMaps is Esri's web tool and public gallery for narratives built from interactive maps, published by governments, universities, humanitarian agencies and newsrooms. Browse it for working examples of map based storytelling and method, remembering that it is a vendor platform with no editorial review of user stories.
what_makes_it_distinct: A very large public gallery of map led narratives, built on the same ArcGIS stack the reader uses at work.

name: Energy Monitor
modifier_reason: Overlaps the climate outlets already listed; status unknown
description: Energy transition news and analysis site launched in 2020 within New Statesman Media Group and later part of GlobalData. It covered power markets, policy and decarbonization data; its current status was not confirmed in this audit, so verify that it still publishes before use.
what_makes_it_distinct: Energy transition coverage built on a commercial data provider's market figures.

name: Gramophone
modifier_reason: Adds music criticism, a thin area in the portfolio
description: Gramophone is a British monthly magazine on classical music founded in 1923 and published by Mark Allen Group, known for its recording reviews and annual awards. Use it to choose recordings and follow performers, with a searchable review archive reaching back a century for subscribers.
what_makes_it_distinct: A century of classical recording reviews in one searchable archive.

name: Jacobin
format: Quarterly print magazine, daily web essays, podcasts, video
modifier_reason: Labour perspective from a nonprofit; openly partisan and overlaps Dissent
description: Jacobin is a socialist magazine founded in 2010 by Bhaskar Sunkara and published in New York by the nonprofit Jacobin Foundation, with a quarterly print edition and daily web commentary. Use it for labour movement coverage, union campaigns and left political economy, reading it as argument from a declared position.
what_makes_it_distinct: The most widely read English language socialist magazine, with steady coverage of strikes and union organizing.

name: Pambazuka News
modifier_reason: African movement voices, but current activity is unconfirmed
description: Pambazuka News is a Pan African platform for commentary and analysis on social justice, founded in 2000 by the organization Fahamu. Use its archive for activist and scholarly writing on human rights, land, gender and governance across Africa, and check whether new issues are still appearing.
what_makes_it_distinct: A long running archive of African activist and movement writing.

name: The Cambodia Daily
modifier_reason: Underserved Cambodia, offset by reduced exile operation and aggregation
description: The Cambodia Daily was an independent Phnom Penh newspaper founded in 1993 by Bernard Krisher that stopped printing in September 2017 after a disputed tax bill. It has continued online from abroad in English and Khmer, largely curating other outlets' reports, so treat it as a secondary source.
what_makes_it_distinct: A newspaper forced out of Cambodia in 2017 that persists as an exile website in English and Khmer.

name: The Syllabus
owner: The Syllabus (founder and publisher Evgeny Morozov)
modifier_reason: Independent and subscriber funded, but a curator of other sources
description: The Syllabus is a curation project founded in 2019 by the technology critic Evgeny Morozov, which uses a mix of algorithms and human editors to select academic papers, essays, talks and podcasts from across the web. Use its themed weekly lists to find serious work on technology, political economy and culture that ranking feeds bury.
what_makes_it_distinct: Human and machine curation that ranks academic and long work by intellectual merit instead of popularity.

name: Tribune
owner: Owner of Islam Channel (acquired 2025, per Press Gazette)
modifier_reason: Labour movement voice; single line, recent ownership change
description: British socialist magazine founded in 1937, relaunched in 2018 under Jacobin's publisher and acquired in 2025 by the owner of Islam Channel. Read it for arguments from the Labour left on unions, housing, public ownership and political economy, as one committed voice among others.
what_makes_it_distinct: The historic magazine of the British Labour left, once edited by Aneurin Bevan and Michael Foot.

name: Jihadica
regions: Middle East and North Africa / Global
owner: Jihadica (founded by William McCants, edited by Cole Bunzel)
format: Expert blog posts, primary source analysis
modifier_reason: Academic expertise, reduced because posting appears close to dormant
description: Jihadica is an academic blog founded in 2008 by William McCants and later edited by Cole Bunzel, in which specialists who read Arabic analyse the texts, debates and internal disputes of jihadi movements. Use its archive for primary source context on ideology, since posting has been infrequent in recent years.
what_makes_it_distinct: Scholars reading jihadi ideological texts in the original Arabic and explaining the internal arguments to outsiders.

name: Mirror Media (鏡週刊)
owner: Mirror Media Inc. (鏡傳媒), founded by Pei Wei (裴偉)
format: Articles, weekly magazine, longform profiles, video
modifier_reason: Tabloid churn; The Reporter covers investigations with stronger method
description: A Taiwanese weekly magazine and news site launched in 2016 by former Next Magazine publisher Pei Wei, mixing political and business scoops with celebrity and crime coverage. Use it selectively for exclusives that shape the Taiwanese news agenda and for its longform profiles, and cross check claims against The Reporter or public media.
what_makes_it_distinct: Taiwan's main scoop driven weekly, whose exclusives on politicians and business figures often drive the national news cycle.

name: Sahan Journal
modifier_reason: Nonprofit, but outside priority geographies; earlier label was wrong
description: Sahan Journal is a nonprofit digital newsroom in Minnesota founded in 2019 by Mukhtar Ibrahim to report for and about immigrants and communities of colour in that state. It is a United States local outlet, not an East African one, so use it mainly as a model of community centred reporting.
what_makes_it_distinct: A local newsroom built by and for immigrant communities, with Somali Minnesotans at its origin.

name: Sahara Reporters
owner: Sahara Reporters Media Group (founder Omoyele Sowore)
modifier_reason: West Africa ground signal, but thin verification standards
description: Sahara Reporters is a Nigerian news site founded in New York in 2006 by the activist Omoyele Sowore, built on leaks and citizen reports about corruption and abuse of power. Use it as an early signal on Nigerian scandals, and confirm claims with Premium Times or wire reports.
what_makes_it_distinct: A diaspora based outlet that publishes leaked documents on Nigerian officials that domestic media often avoid.

name: The Baffler
modifier_reason: Small nonprofit; labour and technology criticism against prevailing hype
description: The Baffler is a magazine of political and cultural criticism founded in 1988 by Thomas Frank and Keith White, now published in New York by the nonprofit Baffler Foundation. Use it for skeptical essays on business culture, technology hype, labour and media, plus fiction and poetry.
what_makes_it_distinct: Satirical, combative criticism of business and technology boosterism from a small nonprofit magazine.

name: The Gradient
modifier_reason: Volunteer academic voice, offset by unclear current activity
description: The Gradient is a volunteer run publication started in 2017 by researchers at the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, offering essays, interviews and a podcast on machine learning research. Use its archive for clear technical overviews, and check how recently it has published before relying on it for news.
what_makes_it_distinct: Long explanatory essays on machine learning written by working researchers for a wider audience.

name: boundary 2
modifier_reason: Academic depth in theory; narrow use for this reader
description: boundary 2 is a quarterly journal of literature and culture founded in 1972 and published by Duke University Press, with a strong tradition in critical theory and postcolonial thought. Consult it selectively for demanding theoretical essays, and see its open online companion b2o for shorter reviews.
what_makes_it_distinct: A journal that helped define postmodern literary theory and still publishes long theoretical interventions.

name: Asia Times
regions: Southeast Asia / Taiwan and Greater China / South Asia / Global
modifier_reason: Opinion heavy; overlaps stronger Asia outlets already listed
description: Asia Times is an English language news and commentary site based in Hong Kong, descended from a Bangkok newspaper founded in 1995 and now owned by Asia Times Holdings. Use it selectively for contrarian analysis of Asian geopolitics, finance and technology, checking claims because commentary outweighs reporting.
what_makes_it_distinct: A pan Asian commentary site with a contrarian finance and strategy slant distinct from Western and state outlets.

name: Dezeen
format: News, project features, video, newsletters, awards
modifier_reason: High volume commercial feed overlapping other architecture titles
description: Dezeen is a London based online magazine of architecture, interiors and design founded in 2006 by Marcus Fairs and owned since 2021 by the Danish group JP/Politiken Media. Skim its daily feed to track new buildings and industry debates, and turn to slower journals for criticism.
what_makes_it_distinct: A very high volume daily feed of new architecture and design projects from around the world.

name: NewMusicBox
format: Essays, interviews, audio and video profiles
modifier_reason: New music niche; current publishing status unclear
description: NewMusicBox is the online magazine of the nonprofit New Music USA, launched in 1999, with composer interviews and essays written largely by working musicians. Use its archive for first person writing on contemporary composition and sound practice in the United States; whether it still commissions new articles could not be confirmed.
what_makes_it_distinct: Decades of long conversations with American composers, written and recorded by practitioners.

name: Responsible Statecraft
modifier_reason: Counterweight to hawkish consensus, but advocacy from one institute
description: The online magazine of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, a Washington think tank founded in 2019 that argues for military restraint and diplomacy. Use it as a deliberate counterweight to interventionist commentary on United States foreign policy, arms spending and lobbying, and read it as advocacy with a declared line.
what_makes_it_distinct: A transpartisan restraint school outlet joining left and conservative critics of United States military intervention.

name: n+1
format: Print issues, online essays, fiction, reviews, books
modifier_reason: Nonprofit, offset by overlap with other American literary reviews
description: n+1 is a Brooklyn magazine of literature, culture and politics founded in 2004 by Keith Gessen, Mark Greif, Benjamin Kunkel, Marco Roth and others, published three times a year by the nonprofit n+1 Foundation. Use it for long essays, fiction and criticism that connect intellectual life with left politics and everyday experience.
what_makes_it_distinct: Long unsigned editorials under the heading The Intellectual Situation, diagnosing the cultural moment in a collective voice.

name: Asterisk Magazine
modifier_reason: Careful essays, but one funding milieu and overlap with Works in Progress
description: Asterisk is a quarterly online and print magazine launched in 2022 and edited by Clara Collier, supported by philanthropy aligned with effective altruism. Use it for long, quantitative essays on AI forecasting, biosecurity, global health, economic growth and science policy, read with its intellectual milieu in mind.
what_makes_it_distinct: Quantitative, forecasting minded essays in which authors show their uncertainty and their numbers.

name: Citizen News (眾新聞)
owner: Citizen News (founded by veteran Hong Kong journalists)
modifier_reason: Believed closed since 2022; archive availability unconfirmed
description: A Hong Kong news site founded in 2017 by veteran journalists and funded by readers, which stopped publishing in January 2022, days after the closure of Stand News. Its address now shows only a farewell message, so treat it as a historical marker of reader funded Hong Kong journalism.
what_makes_it_distinct: A record of reader funded Hong Kong journalism from the years just before and after the national security law.

name: Monthly Review
format: Magazine, essays, book press, companion website
modifier_reason: Independent socialist foundation; a declared tradition absent elsewhere in the list
description: Monthly Review is an independent socialist magazine founded in New York in 1949 by Paul Sweezy and Leo Huberman, published by the Monthly Review Foundation and edited by John Bellamy Foster. Use it for Marxist analysis of capitalism, imperialism, labour and ecology, read as a declared position.
what_makes_it_distinct: The longest continuously published socialist magazine in the United States and a home of ecological Marxism.

name: News in Slow Spanish
regions: Europe / Latin America and Brazil / Global
modifier_reason: Learner pacing for Spanish; no original reporting
description: Weekly subscription programme from Linguistica 360 that discusses the week's news in slowed, clearly spoken Spanish, with transcripts, grammar notes and separate Spain and Latin America editions. Use it for listening practice at intermediate level; it summarizes news and does not report it.
what_makes_it_distinct: Current affairs delivered at learner pace in Spanish, with full transcripts for intermediate listeners.

name: Works in Progress
format: Longform essays, newsletter, podcast, print edition
modifier_reason: Distinct urbanism essays, offset by corporate ownership and one line
description: Works in Progress is a magazine of ideas about economic growth, science, housing and technology, founded in 2020 and published by the payments company Stripe since 2022. Use it for well illustrated explanatory essays on urban form, construction and infrastructure, keeping in mind its pro growth, market liberal stance.
what_makes_it_distinct: Illustrated essays on how things came to work, from housing rules to vaccines, argued from a pro growth stance.

name: AllAfrica
regions: Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
format: Aggregated news, topic and country pages, archive
modifier_reason: Aggregator penalty, partly offset by Francophone African breadth
description: AllAfrica is an aggregator operated by AllAfrica Global Media that republishes several hundred reports a day from African news organizations, governments and agencies in English and French. Use it to scan coverage by country or topic, then judge each item by its original publisher.
what_makes_it_distinct: A single searchable feed of English and French reports from many national African newsrooms.

name: Caribbean News Global
modifier_reason: Caribbean is underserved, offset by aggregation and thin sourcing
description: Caribbean News Global is a free English language news site covering politics, economy, diplomacy and regional institutions across the Caribbean, with much of its output drawn from press releases and commentary. Use it as a scan of regional announcements and verify anything important against primary or local sources.
what_makes_it_distinct: A pan Caribbean feed that gathers government, CARICOM and agency announcements from many small island states in one place.

name: New Scientist
format: Weekly magazine, news, features, podcasts, newsletters
modifier_reason: Overlaps Science, Nature news and Quanta; commercial owner
description: New Scientist is a British weekly science magazine founded in 1956 and owned since 2021 by Daily Mail and General Trust. Use it for quick, readable news on research, technology, health and environment, then follow its references to the journals for anything that matters to your work.
what_makes_it_distinct: A weekly digest of research news across all sciences, written for general readers rather than specialists.

name: The Strad
modifier_reason: Deep music niche with narrow relevance to the reader
description: The Strad is a London monthly magazine for string players, teachers and instrument makers, published since 1890 and now part of Newsquest Specialist Media. Use it for interviews, technique articles, concert reviews and detailed studies of violin making, a narrow field it covers in depth.
what_makes_it_distinct: The long standing magazine of bowed string instruments, including technical posters documenting historic violins.

name: Caribbean News Service
modifier_reason: Caribbean gap, but opaque ownership and unconfirmed activity
description: Caribbean News Service is a regional news outlet that reports on politics, business, climate and disaster risk across Caribbean states, and its own website could not be confirmed in this audit. Treat it as a possible supplementary Caribbean feed and check that it is still publishing before relying on it.
what_makes_it_distinct: A regional Caribbean news feed that also appears in the PreventionWeb directory of disaster risk organizations.

name: Musical America
format: Industry news, annual directory, special reports, awards
modifier_reason: Trade focus on the United States; overlaps Bachtrack for this reader
description: Musical America is the oldest American classical music publication, founded in 1898, now an online trade news service and annual International Directory of the Performing Arts. Use it for industry appointments, orchestra and opera finances, artist management and its annual awards, with a strong United States emphasis.
what_makes_it_distinct: The performing arts trade's standing directory of artists, managers, presenters and orchestras, issued every year.

name: Nautilus
modifier_reason: Overlaps other science and ideas magazines already listed
description: Nautilus is an American science magazine launched in 2013 that publishes long essays and reported features linking physics, biology, neuroscience and philosophy. Read it for carefully written explanatory pieces by scientists and writers, with a metered paywall and a print edition for members.
what_makes_it_distinct: Science writing organized around ideas and narrative, with commissioned illustration for each piece.

name: Sentient Media
modifier_reason: Niche beat, though climate nonprofits partly cover it
description: Sentient is a nonprofit news organization, formerly styled Sentient Media, that reports on factory farming, food systems and their links to climate, public health and animal welfare. Treat it as a specialist source on agriculture and climate policy, noting that it grew out of animal protection advocacy.
what_makes_it_distinct: One of very few newsrooms devoted entirely to animal agriculture and its climate footprint.

name: Sixth Tone
modifier_reason: State owned; reported tightening of editorial control
description: Sixth Tone is an English language outlet launched in 2016 by Shanghai United Media Group, a state owned publisher, with features on Chinese society, rural life, labour and culture. Read it for human scale detail that foreign correspondents miss, knowing that politically sensitive subjects are avoided or censored.
what_makes_it_distinct: State owned yet feature driven, showing everyday China in English from inside the system.

name: The Marginalian
modifier_reason: Reader funded single author project; adds reflection, not reporting
description: The Marginalian is the solo publication of the writer Maria Popova, begun in 2006 as Brain Pickings and renamed in 2021, funded by reader donations and free of advertising. Use it for reflective essays that draw passages from literature, philosophy, science and art, as slow reading and not as news.
what_makes_it_distinct: One author's two decade archive of annotated reading across literature, science and philosophy, free and without advertising.

name: Geopolitical Monitor
modifier_reason: Overlaps stronger analysis outlets; thin published standards
description: An international intelligence publication and consultancy based in Toronto that issues situation reports, backgrounders and contributed opinion on strategic risks. Use it as a quick scan of emerging security and economic flashpoints from a Canadian publisher, and verify claims elsewhere because contributor quality varies and editorial standards are thinly documented.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Canadian open source intelligence publisher offering short situation reports on underreported flashpoints.

name: Popula
owner: Popula (owned by its journalists; member of the Brick House Cooperative)
modifier_reason: Cooperative ownership, offset by apparently sparse recent output
description: Popula is a small magazine of news, essays and culture owned by its journalists, founded in 2018 by Maria Bustillos and later joined to the Brick House Cooperative. Read its archive for idiosyncratic international essays and media criticism, but check how recently it has published before relying on it.
what_makes_it_distinct: An experiment in journalist ownership and permanent archiving that began on a blockchain publishing platform.

name: The Scientist
modifier_reason: Off theme; life science news is covered by stronger outlets
description: The Scientist is a magazine for life science researchers published by LabX Media Group, covering biology, biomedicine, laboratory methods and research careers. Use it occasionally for readable accounts of new findings in the life sciences, which sit outside the core themes of this directory.
what_makes_it_distinct: Written for working life scientists, with attention to laboratory methods and careers.

name: VnExpress International
owner: FPT Corporation (licensed under a Vietnamese government ministry)
modifier_reason: Priority country with few alternatives; state supervised press
description: VnExpress International is the English edition of VnExpress, Vietnam's most read online newspaper, owned by the technology company FPT and licensed by a government ministry. Use it for business, society and everyday life in Vietnam, knowing that political coverage follows the official line.
what_makes_it_distinct: The widest English language window on daily Vietnamese life from inside the country's licensed press.

name: IAI News (Institute of Art and Ideas)
owner: The Institute of Art and Ideas
format: Essays, filmed debates, talks, festival recordings
modifier_reason: Overlaps stronger philosophy essay platforms already listed
description: IAI News is the online magazine of the Institute of Art and Ideas, the British organization founded by philosopher Hilary Lawson that also runs the HowTheLightGetsIn festival. It pairs short essays with filmed debates among philosophers and scientists, useful for sampling disputes but often framed provocatively.
what_makes_it_distinct: Filmed debates that put philosophers and scientists who disagree on the same stage.

name: Esprit critique
modifier_reason: Probable duplicate of Esprit; current activity unclear
description: Esprit critique is a French language online journal of sociology and social sciences, founded in 1999 by the Quebec sociologist Jean-François Marcotte and published in thematic issues with free access. It is distinct from the Paris review Esprit, and its recent publishing activity could not be confirmed.
what_makes_it_distinct: An early open access Francophone sociology journal, born online in Quebec in 1999.

name: gal-dem
modifier_reason: Closed in 2023; archive only
description: gal-dem was a London magazine founded in 2015 by Liv Little and written by women and non binary people of colour, which stopped publishing in March 2023. Its website stayed online as an archive of essays on culture, identity and British politics, useful for research but no longer current.
what_makes_it_distinct: Eight years of British culture and politics written entirely by women and non binary people of colour.

name: Puck
modifier_reason: Insider prestige with a United States focus outside the priorities
description: Puck is a subscription media company launched in 2021 whose named writers, who hold equity in the firm, send newsletters on power in Wall Street, Washington, Silicon Valley, Hollywood, media, fashion and art. It is insider reporting for a United States elite audience and sits far from this reader's priorities.
what_makes_it_distinct: Journalists are part owners and are paid partly by the subscribers their own newsletters attract.

name: Resilience.org
modifier_reason: Largely an aggregator with a single advocacy line
description: Resilience.org is a website run by the nonprofit Post Carbon Institute that republishes and commissions articles on energy descent, local economies, food systems and community responses to climate change. Skim it occasionally for perspectives on degrowth and adaptation, checking original sources because much of it is aggregated.
what_makes_it_distinct: A long running digest of post growth and community resilience writing from many small publishers.

name: Morning Brew
modifier_reason: Aggregator; redundant with FT and Reuters; American business focus
description: Morning Brew is a free daily business newsletter from the United States, majority owned by Axel Springer, that summarizes markets, technology and corporate news in a light tone. Use it only as a quick scan, since it aggregates reporting done elsewhere and centres on American business.
what_makes_it_distinct: A conversational five minute digest of American business news.

name: Loop News Caribbean
modifier_reason: Closed in July 2025; no confirmed archive
description: Loop News was a digital news network with editions for many Caribbean territories, owned by the telecom company Digicel, which shut it down in July 2025 after eleven years. It no longer publishes, so the reader should rely on The Gleaner, Barbados Today and Nation News for daily Caribbean coverage.
what_makes_it_distinct: A telecom owned regional news network whose 2025 closure removed a daily source for many small islands.
